main_body: Cottage: a large terracotta tiled roof slope (rows 2-43) over a cream half-timbered front wall with a door and a window (rows 44-79)
top_band: Salmon to terracotta roof tile slope, rows ~3-37, with a darker red eave band at rows 38-43
evidence: The roof is a big tiled slope seen from above, taking about 40 rows. It ends in a dark red eave band at rows 38-43 that shades the wall below, and the chimney sits on the slope. Below it the plaster front has timber framing, a door with a stone surround, and a window with shutters and a sill, all inset. A grey stone base closes the bottom. This matches the reference houses, whose roofs are also large slopes over a front wall. Both the top surface and the south face read clearly.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tile tones with per-tile highlights and dark joints, and the plaster wall is speckled. The timber, door planks, shutters and stone base each have their own ramp. Outlines are dark red-brown beside the roof and dark brown beside the wood, not neutral black. It is a little less rich than the references, which have stronger roof highlights and more varied stone, but it would sit acceptably next to them.
